To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a new advanced adaptive restraint design was developed to better protect automobile passengers in frontal and obliqued motor vehicle crashes.

The new advanced adaptive restraint design with dual volume airbag and knee airbag and switchable dual load limiters has improved performances for occupant injuries reduction than the baseline restraint system, for all considered load cases, and the injury risk reductions vary from case to case, within 8%66%.

a new adaptive restraint system was developed, with the controllable dual volume airbag and tunable vents in the airbag and the knee airbag, and with the updated seatbelt system with switchable dual load limiters, to achieve the good performances for all the fourteen crash scenarios defined in this study with the three body size ATDs and the three body size HMs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of new advanced adaptive restraint systems for the passenger side of the automobile.

the development of a new adaptive passenger restraint concept design and the optimization of the adaptive restraint system configuration for the fourteen load cases representing the real world crash scenarios.

the development of the new advanced adaptive passenger restraints with improved adaptivity, better performances and reduced injury risks for the occupants of different body sizes, seated in different positions and under different crash scenarios.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed new adaptive restraint design is an effective approach for the development of new restraint designs with improved performance for the protection of the passenger occupants in frontal and obliquely frontal crashes.

the proposed new adaptive restraint design has a better adaptivity to occupant size, seating positions and crash scenarios, which is more versatile and effective in reducing occupant injury risks than the current production retracts.
the new adaptive restraint design is a significant improvement over the current restraint systems, and it is ready for further engineering and testing to be used in production vehicles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the advanced adaptive restraint system design with controllable dual volumes of the airbags and knee airbag, tunable venting, switchable load limiters and shoulder and lap pretentioners, has been developed and optimized to achieve better performance for the fourteen load cases.

we developed the new concept designs for a controllable dual volume passenger airbag and knee airbag, integrated them with the updated seatbelt system to form a new advanced adaptive passenger restraint system.
the new adaptive restraint system is capable of achieving good performances in the considered load cases and the new restraint design is a good candidate for further development and validation.

the new adaptive restraint system can be optimized to achieve good performances for all the fourteen considered cases with ATD sled models, and the good performances were verified with the HM sled models.
